subject: Post-incident: RCA summary, timeline, and next-step commitments (Aquifer)
summary: Customer-facing RCA and action plan after the July 29 inference degradation that affected request latency and partial failures for Aquifer Health. Includes timeline, root cause, mitigations, and verification steps.
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Li <alex@aquifer.io>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident: RCA summary, timeline, and next-step commitments (Aquifer)

Alex —

Following our call this morning, attaching the customer-facing RCA and an evidence bundle. I wanted to summarize the key points up front so your engineering and compliance teams can scan quickly: 

- Impact: Between 2028-07-29T21:12:00Z and 2028-07-29T22:44:00Z, Aquifer experienced elevated generation latency and 5xx error surface on the /v1/generate endpoint for ~17% of requests. No data exfiltration detected.
- Root cause (short): A combination of a kernel selection regression in the inference runtime and an aggressive autoscale cooldown that prevented capacity from recovering rapidly under a burst of long-sequence requests.
- Mitigations taken: rolled back kernel selector 1.4.2 -> 1.4.0, reduced cooldown to 30s, enabled priority routing to stable pool for Aquifer's dedicated routes.
- Next steps (we will): (1) prod-only validation run of kernel selector on a shadow cluster, (2) a configuration guard to limit sequence-length spikes from a single tenant, (3) a verification window with you on Aug 2 (proposed).

Attachments: aquifer-rca-2028-07-30.pdf (RCA + timeline + action register), timeline-evidence-logs.zip (sanitized traces & KPIs).

If you prefer a redacted one‑page summary for your legal/compliance folder, we can provide that by EOD. Thanks again for the quick sync — appreciate Alex and the Aquifer team for the patience and the clear repro notes.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0116

---

From: Alex Li <alex@aquifer.io>

Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-incident: RCA summary, timeline, and next-step commitments (Aquifer)

Neha —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear doc. A couple quick clarifying Qs from our SREs: 
1) Can you share the short-lived autoscale metrics that show why cooldown blocked recovery? We only need aggregated graphs (no raw tokens).
2) The timeline references the kernel selector change that rolled out at 20:58 UTC — can you confirm whether that rollout was staggered by region?

We'd like to take the RCA to our CSAT committee on Thursday; if you can provide the one-page redacted summary by EOD tomorrow that would be ideal. Also please confirm the proposed Aug 2 verification window (we're available 14:00–16:00 PDT).

Alex
Head of Engineering, Aquifer Health
alex@aquifer.io

> On Mon, 30 Jul 2028 at 09:15, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > Following our call this morning, attaching the customer-facing RCA...

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Li <alex@aquifer.io>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, productops@aquifer.io, support@aquifer.io
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-incident: RCA summary, timeline, and next-step commitments (Aquifer)

Alex —

Appreciate the questions. Quick answers inline: 
1) Autoscale graphs: included in timeline-evidence-logs.zip as "autoscale-aggregates.png" (sanitized 1m resolution). Those show the pool did not scale to target for ~13 minutes because the cooldown prevented new nodes from joining during repeated eviction cycles.
2) Kernel selector rollout: it was a single control-plane rollout targeting global pools; however the selector heuristic interacts differently with some A100-optimized kernels, which is what produced the regression on large-seq workloads. So effect was observed in our us-west and eu-central pools first.

We will produce the one-page redacted summary by EOD tomorrow (Jul 31) and confirm Aug 2 verification (14:00–15:00 PDT preferred).

Action items captured in the attached RCA: 
- Infra: automatic rollback guard for kernel-selector changes (owner: irene_choi) — target Aug 6
- Runtime: implement tenant sequence-length caps and runtime telemetry (owner: dylan_brooks) — target Aug 9
- CS: provide redacted customer summary and coordinate verification slot (owner: neha_kapoor) — target Jul 31

I'll follow up with calendar invites and the redacted summary.

Best,
Neha
